new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, no existing statement supplied in the bundle). The deposit adds transcription evidence pointing to word-final primary stress with a secondary stress earlier in the word; it states no rule. Two bibliography rows are tagged 'read: notes on stress' (HRELP project page 2005-2007; Reis 2023) but their statements are not in the bundle and their copies we hold were not yet in the mirror at, so no comparison with them could be made here.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The deposit contains NO prose statement about stress (no sketch grammar or phonology document is among its 138 bundles; the deposit-level metadata and Brandão et al. 2023 section 5 say nothing about prosody). What it does contain is primary data bearing on stress: the open Swadesh-list PDF 'compiled for phonological analysis' gives phonetic transcriptions with IPA-style stress marks, and in the Enawene-Nawe columns the primary-stress mark stands before the word-FINAL syllable in the great majority of marked forms (my count over the first transcribed form of each row: consultant Holikiari column 46 final vs 5 penultimate among 51 marked forms; 'Ubiray' column 56 final vs 8 penultimate among 64 marked; e.g. na'to 'I', e'ɾe 'he', wi'ʃu 'we', eta'ko 'that', nowa'ka 'here', halako'ta 'where', hane'ra 'when', e'na 'man', kaxo'lo 'dog', e'se 'seed', tewẽ:'na 'heavy', ataj'ɾa 'tree', ene'te 'meat', ini'ɦũ 'tail/feather'). Reading 'fixed: final syllable' is therefore an inference from the depositor's transcriptions, not a rule stated by the work; roughly half of the rows (compounds, phrases, orthographic forms) carry no stress mark at all.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Transcriptions mark a secondary stress (low comma / IPA ̩) on an earlier syllable of longer words, e.g. i,kʲaʃi'ʃi 'small/few', a,ko'te 'many', eta'ta 'bark/skin', ene'te 'meat', ene'se 'egg', he,nene'ɦẽ, we,se'koti, de ̩ʃo 'you (pl)'; no statement of a rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated (no prose). Penultimate-marked forms in the data: ko'ɦãse ~kõ'ɦãse 'fish', u'ɦiɾʊ 'woman' (older speakers' form, Ubiray column; Holikiari column uɦiɾu/owiro unmarked), ha'nera 'when' in the Ubiray column vs hane'ra in the Holikiari column, e'kãnʊ, we,se'koti, mata'nali, ha'kina.
new_statements.identity_note: Enawene-Nawe (ISO unk) as spoken at Halataikwa village (deposit coordinates -12.18, -59.12; Brandão et al. 2023: c. 1000 speakers in Halataikwa and Kolinakwa, Mato Grosso); Swadesh list consultant Holikiari Enawe(ne), recorded 2019-04-02; the middle column 'Ubiray' reproduces forms from Ubiray Rezende's earlier work; the first column is Paresi (consultant Genivaldo Zezokaece), not this language.

sources.note: Enawene-Nawe inventory (pp. 64-65) and syllable types (pp. 130-131, Tabelas 5a/5b) after Rezende (2003, pp. 132-135). No stress rule stated for Enawene-Nawe. The reproduced transcriptions show final primary stress with alternating secondary stresses leftward ([ˌa.ko.ˈla], [ˌha.ma.ˌka.te.ˈne] 'esfrie-o', [hĩ.ˌʃi.ʃa.ˈse], [ˌa.niː.ˈnĩ] 'ele comeu', [ˌke.te.ˈkʷwa] 'roça'), plus non-final cases [aj.ˌɾaw.wa.ˈkeː.na] 'fala durante o sono' (penult, long V) and [ˈdĩ.ɲwa] 'criança'.
